summary: Tenant prefetch saturation caused connection queue growth and elevated 5xx/502 wave
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled batch ingestion from customer Bytewave (dedicated tenant) we observed a rapid spike in gateway 5xx responses (predominantly 502/503) and downstream serving-runtime restarts between 15:20–15:36 UTC. The first alert came from the customer's monitoring: a sustained 502 rate for their tenant route and degraded streaming session success.

Impact:
- Bytewave experienced elevated request failures for ~16 minutes; some webhook ingestion jobs failed and retried causing client-level backlog.
- Internal metrics: 502 rate for tenant route increased from baseline ~0.1% to ~8% at peak.
- Several serving-runtime pods restarted with OOMKilled and watchdog reset logs.

Environment:
- prod cluster (us-west primary), dedicated pool assigned to Bytewave (pool-id: dbw-ded-07).
- Model route: redwood-v1-13b (tenant pinned), prefetch enabled (prefix prefetch + KV cache).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Bytewave kicked off a mass ingestion that triggered high prefetch concurrency against pinned model routes.
2) API gateway connection queue length increased as backpressure propagated to runtime.
3) Serving runtime started heavy KV cache churn; memory fragmentation and GPU memory allocations rose.
4) Runtime processes OOM/killed and restarted; gateway observed unhealthy upstreams and returned 502/503.

Observed behavior:
- API gateway returned 502/503 and occasional 504 when connection timeouts occurred.
- Runtime logs show frequent lines: "kv_cache: eviction thrash detected" and "gpu_alloc failed: out of memory".
- Autoscaler briefly attempted to add nodes but warmup and placement delayed capacity, amplifying the 5xx wave.

Expected behavior:
- Tenant prefetch should be rate-limited to prevent upstream overload, and connector should fallback to a safe cached variant rather than thrash KV cache.

Relevant logs & dashboards:
- Console dashboard: https://console.redwood.com/d/tenant-ops/bytewave-502s (graph snapshots attached in ticket)
- Runtime pod logs (snippet): "E0310 15:25:12 kv_cache.cc:312] eviction thrash, loop=37"
- Gateway traces: trace-id=trace-0a1b2c (attached)

Notes on customer impact and outreach:
- Customer support notified Bytewave at 15:28 UTC and provided temporary mitigation steps.
- Finance/CS escalation: customer indicated retries caused delayed downstream billing batch; CS requested timeline and root-cause analysis.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:29 - Aisha Patel (Support): Initial triage — saw tenant route 502 spike, opening incident. Asked SRE to pull runtime pod logs and recent autoscaler events.

2026-03-10 15:33 - SRE (Maria Chen): Observed rapid increase in prefetch request rate from tenant agent. KV cache eviction counters jumped 250x; multiple runtimes reported OOMKilled. Pushing tests to reproduce in staging.
2026-03-10 15:41 - Customer (Bytewave Ops): Confirmed they started an internal backfill job at ~15:18 UTC that batched ~10k requests/min for ~3 minutes. They've paused the job at 15:30 UTC.

2026-03-10 16:05 - Liam O'Connor (Assignee): Applied emergency mitigation: disabled tenant prefix prefetch on the dedicated pool and bumped tenant concurrency limit from 200 to 50. Immediate reduction in 502 rate observed. Need follow-up patch for controlled prefetch rate limiter.

2026-03-11 09:12 - Engineering (SRE): Reproduced in staging by running synthetic prefetch generator at 4x production concurrency. Identified that eviction policy thrashes when combined with large model KV footprints; triggers GPU allocation failures. Filing follow-up fix tickets.
2026-03-12 14:22 - CS (Nina Park): Customer accepted temporary mitigation; asked for ETA on permanent fix and whether any billing credits will be issued. Escalated to Sales Ops for credit discussion.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses tested:
- Hypothesis A: Tenant-level prefetch burst exceeded per-tenant concurrency controls. Evidence: request rate from tenant agent exceeded configured soft limits; prefetch worker spawned many parallel requests.
- Hypothesis B: KV cache eviction policy is not resilient to large working sets and sequential prefetch churn. Evidence: eviction counters high, eviction loop seen in logs, and GPU memory fragmentation.
- Hypothesis C: Autoscaler warmup delays and noisy neighbor effects amplified the outage window. Evidence: scale events logged but warm nodes not ready before OOM cycles ended.

Findings:
- Confirmed prefetch concurrency is the root trigger. When prefetch bursts hit the dedicated pool, KV cache churn caused repeated large allocations; runtimes OOM and exit. API gateway marks upstream as unhealthy and returns 502.
- Warmup latency of new nodes contributed but was secondary.

Diagnostics & artifacts:
- Heap and GPU memory flamegraphs attached to Confluence page.
- Repro script: github.com/redwood/testing/replicate-prefetch-spike (internal).
- Related incidents: SUP-26104 (kvcache thrashing) - similar symptom set but different trigger pattern.
resolution_notes:
Workarounds applied:
- 2026-03-10 15:40 UTC: Disabled tenant prefix prefetch for Bytewave on their dedicated pool (immediate relief).
- 2026-03-10 15:45 UTC: Reduced tenant concurrency cap on gateway route from 200 to 50. Observed drop in error rate to near baseline within 6 minutes.

Permanent remediation (plan):
1) Short-term patch (PR #4521): introduce per-tenant prefetch rate limiter and backoff when eviction counters exceed threshold. (Targeted rollout: canary on 2026-03-15).
2) Improve KV cache eviction policy to avoid thrashing for large working sets; landed design doc and follow-up PR #380 for serving-runtime (ETA Q2 2026).
3) Enhance autoscaler warmup heuristics and pre-warm placement for dedicated pools with pinned large models.
4) Add tenant-level observability and a prefetch budget on Console so operators and customers can see prefetch consumption.

Customer communication:
- Informed Bytewave of immediate mitigation and proposed timeline for fix. CS to coordinate any service credit requests with Sales Ops.

Follow-ups / Action items:
- ENG-7892: Implement rate limiter and add e2e test for prefetch saturation (owner: serving-runtime team).
- SRE-4123: Add dashboard tile for per-tenant prefetch usage and KV eviction alerts.
- CS-2011: Outreach and potential billing remediation conversation.

Related artifacts:
- PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4521 (prefetch limiter)
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Prefetch+Budget+Design
resolution: Mitigated (temporary) and planned permanent fixes. Incident closed for active recovery; follow-up work assigned.
